title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 69-71): in this third version of 'Analysis situs', Grothendieck is axiomatizing a set M of 'strates' (strata) with three relations. X ≤ Y means X is an incidence/boundary face of Y. X ≪ Y means inclusion. X ≬ Y means compatibility. He also wants a notion of 'support'. Page 69 doubts that 'support' makes sense outside the quasi-set-theoretic case. It then works out the test example of a totally ordered set I. M0 = I (the points, or 0-strata). M1 = the closed subsegments [a,b], a<b (the 1-strata), with ∂[a,b] = {a,b}. Two strata are compatible iff (a) they are equal, (b) one is an endpoint of the other, or (c) they are disjoint or meet in a single common endpoint. All axioms hold except Ax 1 (divisibility), which holds iff every open interval ]a,b[ is nonempty, i.e. I is dense.

This page (70) records the following.
(i) These structures are finite combinatorial objects. Elements of M0 have dimension 0 and elements of M1 have dimension 1. The 'boundary set' X̃ (strata strictly below X for ≤) has cardinality 0 for a point and 2 for a segment.
(ii) The admissible 'figures' 𝓕 are the finite subsets F ⊂ M that are closed under ≤ (they contain both endpoints of each segment) and pairwise compatible. In modern terms these are finite 1-dimensional subdivided complexes embedded in the line I, i.e. finite unions of isolated points and subdivided segments, as drawn.
(iii) A retrospective, self-critical remark on an earlier text 'CF III'. There he had carefully defined the support of such an object as a subset of I, which he called 'modérée fermée' (tame closed). He says he should have called these simply 'modérée' (tame), and should have called 'constructible' what he had called 'modérée'. This gives a reasonable formalization for finite sets of figures.
(iv) For infinite families, things are fine if I is a 'tronçon adonné' (a technical notion of CF III, p. 8). There one still has:
- a notion of constructible subsets of I;
- complements of such subsets;
- a compatibility relation between constructible subsets;
- a good formalism of ∪, ∩, complement for pairwise compatible families (X_α), where compatible means the union of the ∂X_α is 'totally adonnée'.

Page 71 continues with a formulation that makes no hypothesis on I. Supports are taken in the finite Boolean algebra on the 'points' {a1}, ]a1,a2[, {a2}, …, {an} attached to a finite chain Δ ⊂ I. This is a cell decomposition of a 'tame' line subordinate to Δ, which handles the case where ]a,b[ is empty.

Purpose: test whether the abstract strata/support axioms for a tame ('modérée') topology behave correctly on the simplest 1-dimensional model, an arbitrary ordered set.
errors: No genuine mathematical error. There is only a slight looseness: closure under ≤ plus pairwise compatibility does not by itself force F to be a 'subdivision'. Two segments sharing an endpoint are allowed, while overlapping segments are excluded, as intended. So figures are exactly finite 1-dimensional subdivided subcomplexes of I, which is fine.
The meaning of 'tronçon adonné' and 'totalement adonnée' depends on CF III, which is not available here. The compatibility criterion for infinite families cannot be checked independently.

ideas.what: Figures in an ordered set I: finite ≤-closed, pairwise compatible sets of points and closed segments (finite 1-dim cell complexes in a line)
ideas.modern_name: finite 1-dimensional (regular) cell complexes / face posets; cell decomposition of a 1-dim tame space
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (combinatorial topology); in tame setting, o-minimal cell decomposition (Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn, van den Dries, 1984-86)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 only sketches 'topologie modérée' without this formalism

ideas.what: Renaming: 'modérée' sets should be called 'constructible'; Boolean algebra (∪, ∩, complement) of constructible subsets of a line, generated by points and intervals
ideas.modern_name: interval algebra of a linear order; definable sets of an o-minimal structure in dimension 1 (finite unions of points and intervals)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mostowski–Tarski (interval algebras, 1939); o-minimality: van den Dries 1984, Pillay–Steinhorn 1986
ideas.where_published: terminology 'constructible' is from EGA (constructible sets in Zariski topology); the tame version is unpublished

ideas.what: Abstract strata structure with three relations (incidence ≤, inclusion ≪, compatibility ≬) and supports, tested on ordered sets including non-dense ones (divisibility axiom fails iff some ]a,b[ is empty)
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic tame topology / stratified spaces via incidence posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: no standard attribution; related to o-minimal structures and to exit-path/stratified poset formalisms
ideas.where_published: only announced programmatically in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

missed.claim: In June 1986, Grothendieck independently builds, on an arbitrary ordered set I, the 'constructible = finite unions of points and intervals' Boolean algebra and its cell decompositions. This is the 1-dimensional core of o-minimality, which Pillay–Steinhorn were publishing the same year. He also explicitly handles non-dense orders, where ]a,b[ = ∅. The link between his 'topologie modérée' program and o-minimality is often asserted retrospectively; this page shows concretely how close his formalism was, and where it differs: incidence-poset axioms rather than first-order definability.
missed.quote: alors que j'aurais dû dire "modérée" tout court, et appeler constructibles les parties que j'appelle "modérées"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents the precise form of Grothendieck's tame-topology axiomatics for historians. It could also inform combinatorial or order-theoretic versions of o-minimality over arbitrary (non-dense) orders.

deep.surprise_reason: A worked elementary example (points and segments of an ordered set) and a terminological self-correction. The mathematics is routine; the interest is only in documenting the unpublished tame-topology axiomatics and its parallel with contemporaneous o-minimality.
transcription_corrections: 'X, Y ∈ F ⇒ X ≢ Y [?]' should be read as the compatibility relation X ≬ Y (the \between symbol from p. 69), not a non-equivalence.

'j'ai pris la peine en intellectuel [?] de définir la notion d'un tel objet' likely reads 'j'ai pris la peine consciencieusement de définir le support d'un tel objet comme partie de I' (the support is what is defined as a subset of I).
'c'est 𝔐 si I est un tronçon adonné' likely reads 'c'est OK si I est un tronçon adonné'.

'dans le cas justement [?] d'un ens{+emble+} de figures' likely reads 'dans le cas d'un ens. fini de figures' (with 'finis' inserted above the line), contrasted with 'Dans le cas d'un ensemble infini' in the next sentence.
'des ∂X_α soit tot^t adonnée' - 'totalement adonnée' is correct as read.
